svg.aria-label: Share of tasks economically exposed to AI in 36 African countries. South Africa is highest at 51.0% and South Sudan lowest at 3.3%, against an African average of 24.6% and 41.4% across all 124 measured countries. The measure is the share of tasks rated 2 or 3 on a 0-3 exposure scale under each country's conditions, not a share of jobs.
svg.text: Share of tasks economically exposed to AI, under country conditions
The paper's economic-exposure threshold: tasks rated 2 or 3 on a 0-3 scale, labelled per country. Not a share of jobs.
Garg, Crosta and Baier (2026), Global Automation Atlas, country panel; exposure is coded 0-3.
Levels 2-3 are economically exposed; level 1 is assistive contact and level 0 has no contact.
Tasks are relabelled under each country's conditions on a common task universe, not weighted by employment.
This is not a share of jobs. Bold country names are the ten countries tracked elsewhere in this record.
